summary.headline: Natco Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR794.4 crores (from INR1,390.6 crores) on lower Lenalidomide, while Adcock associate profit share jumped to INR84.3 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue declined sharply year-on-year to INR794.4 crores, mainly due to lower Lenalidomide sales, partly offset by double-digit growth in the base business. EBITDA including other income was INR245.7 crores (30.9% margin), improving quarter-on-quarter on international and domestic performance and lower operating costs. Consolidated PAT was INR206.5 crores versus INR269 crores in Q4 FY26, which included a one-time INR115 crore deferred tax benefit; management said normalised PAT grew 34% QoQ. Management reiterated FY27 PAT guidance of around INR750 crores and cautioned against annualising the flu-season-boosted Adcock contribution.

segments.name: International formulations
segments.commentary: INR477 crores in the quarter, down QoQ; Brazil grew 180% to INR178 crores on oncology portfolio, Canada about INR56 crores. Management did not split rest-of-world.

segments.name: Domestic formulations
segments.commentary: INR136 crores; base business about INR130 crores vs about INR107 crores normal, helped by semaglutide and third-party orders. Management expects domestic volumes to grow about 25% this year.

segments.name: Associate: Adcock Ingram (South Africa)
segments.commentary: Associate revenue INR1,582.8 crores and PAT INR242.2 crores; NATCO share INR84.3 crores on 35.75% holding, boosted by strong flu season. Stake raised by 13.25% in July 2026 to 49%.

segments.name: Crop Health Sciences
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR40 crores with an EBITDA loss; FY26 revenue about INR138 crores. Management targets EBITDA breakeven for FY27 and a stronger Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of around INR750 crores retained; management said it is not changing guidance and advised against annualising Q1 Adcock profit.
FY27 gross sales guided at INR3,300-3,400 crores (unchanged), with Crop Health revenue of about INR750 crores for the year as previously stated.
Crop Health Sciences expected to break even for FY27; Q2 expected to be significantly better than Q1.
Domestic formulation volumes expected to rise about 25% this year.
Two US launches expected in the next financial year, to be launched with exclusivity; carfilzomib launch on track, timing to be confirmed closer to launch date.
Organic capex about INR250-300 crores per year.
Crop Health demerger now likely around March (about 2-3 months later than December) because of the proposed fundraise.
NATCO product registrations in South Africa via Adcock filed (three dossiers); launch expected around 2028.
Semaglutide filing not made in Canada or Brazil; South Africa dossier still some way off.
capex_capacity: Carfilzomib plant under upgrade; completion expected by end of calendar 2026, and launch to follow once US launch date is set.
Organic capex run-rate about INR250-300 crores per year.
Management plans ANDA filings of 8-10 per year and 2-3 FTF filings per year; expects at least one or two FTF filings this year.
Crop Health portfolio of about 35 products, 8 CTPR-related; CTPR contributes an estimated 30-35% of Crop Health revenue; CTPR technical exports have started but are not significant.
demand_pricing: Semaglutide market in India described as cutthroat and pricing still settling; the brand earns about INR2 crores per month, with some third-party volumes not expected to repeat. It does not lose money but makes little profit.
Adcock profit spike driven by a strong South African flu season, which management called cyclical.
Lenalidomide revenue was negligible in Q1 FY27.
Crop Health sales hit by El Nino concerns and delayed rains, which pushed back the cropping season.
Brazil growth driven by the oncology portfolio; management expects further launches in FY27 subject to patent litigation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the INR2,000 crore fundraise planned, given the existing cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Net cash is around INR1,400 crores after about INR3,000 crores of investments over the last year, mainly Adcock. Funds are needed for short-term loans, capex and two acquisition opportunities (one in India, one outside). QIP, rights issue or other options are being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PAT guidance of about INR750 crores still valid, given Adcock contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept guidance at around INR750 crores. It said the Q1 Adcock bump was seasonal, normal profit is around INR100 crores per quarter at the 100% level, and asked analysts not to annualise the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall sharply QoQ and YoY, and is this the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Last year's Q1 had high R&D and legal costs. R&D spend is lumpy and tied to batches and trials, so this quarter is not the run-rate. Spend will be higher in future quarters, and management suggested an annual view.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: India effective rate is about 25.16% under the new regime, about 27% after disallowances such as CSR. Q1 was higher because Brazil contributed more profit at above 35% tax rate.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Health reach breakeven and what is its revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects breakeven for the year and a much stronger Q2. Q1 revenue was about INR40 crores against INR138 crores in FY26; guidance was not updated beyond the existing FY27 targets.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for South Africa, and can NATCO increase its stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites synergies: NATCO pipeline distribution through Adcock and Indian partner alliances, with value expected in 2-3 years. Bidvest holds 51% and is not selling; NATCO has a first right of refusal but no near-term opportunity.

risks_watch: Adcock Ingram profit is seasonal (flu season); management asked analysts not to annualise the Q1 share of INR84.3 crores, so the INR750 crore FY27 PAT guidance depends on normal-quarter Adcock contribution.
Semaglutide India pricing is described as cutthroat and still settling; third-party volumes are not expected to repeat, and management expects pricing stability in the next few months.

Crop Health Sciences: Q1 EBITDA loss, El Nino and delayed rains pushed back the cropping season; breakeven for FY27 and a significantly better Q2 are targets, not yet delivered. Demerger slipped to about March, roughly 2-3 months later than December.

Olaparib litigation: trial date not recalled by management and the exclusivity determination is still open; carfilzomib launch timing not confirmed, with plant upgrade expected by end of calendar 2026.
Proposed INR2,000 crore fundraise (QIP, rights or other options under evaluation) with two acquisition opportunities, one in India and one outside; deployment and target are undisclosed.
Tax rate volatility: Q1 was higher because Brazil, taxed above 35%, contributed more profit; India guided at about 27% including disallowances.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term story and Adcock, but evasive on specifics: management declined to split rest-of-world exports, give Crop Health revenue guidance beyond the existing targets, name the M&A targets, or confirm the olaparib trial date and carfilzomib launch date. Management was firm that FY27 PAT guidance of around INR750 crores stays unchanged and that the Q1 Adcock profit should not be annualised.

adds.what: Carfilzomib plant upgrade (completion expected by end of calendar 2026; launch follows US launch date)
Organic capex run-rate of INR250-300 crore per year (maintenance/growth mix not split)

growth.why: FY27 gross sales guided at INR3,300-3,400 crore and PAT ~INR750 crore reaffirmed, with domestic volumes expected up ~25% and two US launches next year, but Q1 revenue fell ~43% YoY on negligible Lenalidomide and the Adcock profit spike is cyclical, so the outlook is moderately positive rather than strong.
